instructions: Crack the 4 eggs into a bowl, add the salt and beat until fully combined.
Split the rolls open without cutting all the way through. Toast them cut side down in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until lightly golden. Set them aside.
Warm the beans in a small pot over low heat for 3 minutes, stirring now and then.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Pour in the eggs and cook for 3 minutes, until nearly set.
Slide a spatula under the egg and flip it. Cook the other side for 2 minutes. If it breaks, that's fine.
Slide the egg onto a plate and cut it into 4 wedges.
Spread 1/4 cup of beans on the top half of each roll. On the bottom half, put a wedge of egg and 1/4 cup of the salsa verde. Close the rolls.
method_notes: Mexican Food Journal (5.0 from 3 votes) cooks the eggs as one flat pan egg, cuts it into wedges and builds the torta with refried beans and salsa verde; Mama Latina Tips fries the eggs and adds avocado, with no amounts. The list calls for a fried egg and this keeps it, cooked flat in oil. The lead's ranchero cheese is left out to stay dairy-free, and the beans are lard-free to stay vegetarian. All ratings are tiny, so the lead is a fallback.
